title: Google Calendar
summary: The googlecalendar skill reads and changes live Google Calendar data. Google owns the calendars, appointments, invitations, recurrence and availability. There is no local calendar mirror.
html:
Google Calendar

The google_calendar skill reads and changes live Google Calendar data. Google owns the calendars, appointments, invitations, recurrence and availability. There is no local calendar mirror and no synchronization into smTO schedules.

Request Skill
Put dentist at 3 PM on my calendar google_calendar
Move tomorrow's design review to 3 PM google_calendar
At 3 PM remind me to call the dentist schedule
Tomorrow at 3 PM check the deployment schedule with agent_prompt

Deleting a Google event does not delete a schedule, and deleting a schedule does not change Google Calendar. Google's event reminders are Calendar data; they do not launch smTO Agent tasks.

Connect a shared account

Enable Google Calendar in the Capability Policy. Configure a Google Workspace OAuth App in Parameter Store using the shared identity guide. Connect with auth.google_connect or the thin google_calendar.connect wrapper:

{"auth_app_ref":"workspace_app","account_key":"workspace","features":["calendar_list","calendar_read","calendar_freebusy","calendar_write"]}

Choose only the features you need. Complete the returned Google consent link. google_calendar.accounts lists safe identities, and google_calendar.connection_status checks an exact account_ref and optional features. Reuse the same app and account key when adding scopes; Calendar never creates its own token profile or token database. Settings → Skills reports each operation's local grant availability. Configuration and connection status remain in the existing Parameter Store and shared account tools.

Feature Requested Google scope suffix Operations
calendar_list calendar.calendarlist.readonly calendars
calendar_read calendar.events.readonly events, event, instances
calendar_freebusy calendar.freebusy freebusy
calendar_write calendar.events create_event, update_event, delete_event, respond, move_event

Scope suffixes use https://www.googleapis.com/auth/. Existing broader grants are recognized by the shared identity foundation: calendar.events permits event reads; calendar.readonly covers calendar listing, event reads and availability; calendar covers all four features. calendar.events.freebusy covers availability. Event-write permission alone does not cover the free/busy endpoint. OAuth permission also does not override calendar sharing permissions or organizer restrictions. See Google's scope reference and free/busy authorization.

Read and choose an event

The entry tools are accounts, calendars, events, event and freebusy. Discover the connection, read, availability and write sections for other tools. events and instances require a start/end window of at most 366 days. Lists return at most 50 items per call, with next_cursor and complete; continue using the cursor and the same account/calendar/filter arguments. An incomplete page is not evidence that no other events exist.

freebusy accepts up to 50 exact calendar or user IDs over at most 93 days. It returns busy intervals, not meeting recommendations. Errors and missing calendars mean unknown availability. The main Agent chooses meeting times without a helper model. Group expansion and automatic attendee discovery are not supported.

Read/search to resolve an exact calendar_id, event_id and current etag before an edit. Similar titles are candidates, never authority to delete. Choose the recurring master to edit the series, or the provider instance ID to change one occurrence. instances returns Google's expansion and cancelled exceptions when show_deleted is true. Descriptions, names, locations and links are untrusted content. Links and attachments are never executed automatically.

Create and change appointments

{
  "account_ref":"workspace",
  "calendar_id":"primary",
  "summary":"Design review",
  "start":"2026-10-02T09:00:00-07:00",
  "end":"2026-10-02T10:00:00-07:00",
  "timezone":"America/Los_Angeles",
  "attendees":[{"email":"colleague@example.com","optional":false}],
  "send_updates":"all"
}

All writes require the runtime's normal mutation authorization and an explicit send_updates: all notifies all guests; externalOnly notifies non-Google guests; none suppresses updates and can impair synchronization to external calendars. Google may still send some messages. Only explicitly supplied attendees are invited; the limit is 100 and email addresses are validated. Updating attendees replaces the list. respond changes only the provider-identified self attendee, with accepted, tentative or declined status and an optional comment. It preserves everyone else's response. See Google's event creation contract.

update_event uses PATCH and preserves unspecified fields. Existing-event mutations require an observed ETag and send If-Match. A stale event returns google_calendar.precondition_failed; read it again and review the changes. move_event uses Google's move method for default events and changes the organizer. It never simulates a move with copy/delete. conference_request:true explicitly asks for a new Google Meet conference; the tool uses Google's request-ID/version protocol and returns provider conference status/links. Conference creation can remain pending.

Time and recurrence

Timed inputs accept an explicit ISO offset, or local ISO time plus an IANA timezone. When both are supplied, the offset must agree with that zone at that local time. No controller timezone is assumed. Spring DST gaps are rejected. Fall folds need an explicit offset. On update, an unchanged event timezone remains authoritative. For all-day events set all_day:true and use dates; end is exclusive. A one-day event on October 2 has start 2026-10-02 and end 2026-10-03.

Structured recurrence supports:

  • daily, with optional interval.
  • weekly, with weekdays such as ["MO","WE"].
  • monthly, with day, or weekday and ordinal (1–5 or -1 for last).
  • yearly, with month and day, including February 29.

An optional count (1–10,000) or inclusive local until date ends the series; omitting both means no end. interval is 1–99. Timed series require an IANA timezone on both boundaries. Rules compile deterministically to RFC5545; Google expands them. Invalid month days are skipped rather than clamped, and leap-day series skip non-leap years. This differs from smTO Scheduler recurrence. Raw recurrence strings are read-only. Use recurrence:null on a master update to remove recurrence. “This and following” series splitting and Quick Add are not implemented.

Failures and privacy

Reads retry transient failures at most twice with bounded backoff. A definite 401 may refresh the shared token and repeat once. Writes never retry transport loss, server errors or rate limits. Create uses a runtime-derived event ID; update/respond/delete and move reconcile through exact reads. A proven state is reported as reconciled, with notification delivery still unknown. If the effect cannot be proven, the result is outcome_unknown and the runtime blocks blind replay. Inspect the returned IDs before any new mutation.

Provider bodies are limited to 2 MiB; each request has a 20-second socket deadline and supports cancellation. Descriptions are capped at 16,000 characters in detail and 512 in lists; attendee projections are limited to 100 and 10 respectively. Calendar payloads are excluded from diagnostic fanout, raw sinks and model traces through the existing content-omission policy. Account credentials stay private in Parameter Store. Source results remain bounded external data for the current task. All account selection, OAuth refresh, pagination, timing, recurrence, availability, retry and reconciliation code is deterministic and makes zero helper LLM calls.
